mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes V Class V200 or V250 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A V200 or V250 petrol engine replacement typically costs between £1,800 and £4,500 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. M274 2.0-litre turbo units range from £1,800 to £4,500 supply only. Rebuilt M274 (V200 / V250 / V260): £1,800-£4,500 supply only. Reconditioned units: £1,800-£3,200. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£2,800 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the M274 engine in the V Class V200 and V250 reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M274 is considered a fundamentally sound engine, with high-mileage examples common across C-Class, GLC and V-Class platforms. However, it has predictable weak points. Timing chain tensioner wear causing cold-start rattle - the most common issue. High-pressure fuel pump failure on higher-mileage units. Carbon buildup on intake valves (inherent to direct injection). Camshaft actuator wear causing ticking on cold start. Post-2016 engines have improved timing chain components.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M274 timing chain failure in a V Class petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M274's timing chain system typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Rattling or clanking noise on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds. Rough idle and loss of power. Check engine light with cam/crank correlation fault codes. Metallic ticking noise from the engine when warm. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth and destroy the engine.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my V200 or V250 petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner, HPFP, camshaft actuators, carbon cleaning). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. Timing chain replacement at specialist: £1,100-£1,700 - do this at first sign of rattle. HPFP replacement: £500-£800 - do this immediately after first cut-out. Walnut blasting: £300-£500 - preventative every 60,000 miles. Full M274 rebuild: £2,800-£4,500 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given V Class V200 / V250 values (£15,000-£35,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my V200 or V250 has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. V200 / V250 / V260 (2014-present): M274.920 (2.0L turbo, 211hp). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used V200 or V250 petrol engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a V Class petrol. The W447 engine bay layout, 7G-TRONIC gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Engine removal requires proper lifting equipment and subframe lowering. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes V Class V200 / V250 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes V Class V200 and V250 petrol models are powered by the M274 2.0-litre turbocharged engine - a smooth and refined unit shared with the C-Class and GLC. While fundamentally robust, the M274 has developed well-documented weaknesses including timing chain tensioner wear, high-pressure fuel pump failure, and carbon buildup on intake valves. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common V Class petrol engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M274 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the V200 / V250 Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes V Class V200, V250, V260 (M274.920, 2014-present)
problems.rootCause: The M274's timing chain tensioner can lose oil pressure retention when parked, causing chain slack and a characteristic rattle on cold start. If left unaddressed, the chain can stretch and eventually skip teeth with catastrophic valve-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner only, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught very early with no chain stretch

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if rattle is persistent or chain has stretched

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M274 with new timing components, upgraded tensioner, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped or guides have failed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W447 V Class V200 or V250 petrol is worth £15,000-£35,000 depending on age and mileage - the full replacement cost of £2,800-£4,500 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £10,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: At the first sign of rattling on cold start, have the timing chain tensioner inspected immediately. The M274 timing chain is a known weak point - ignoring it can lead to complete engine failure. On a V Class with over 90,000 miles, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is often the most cost-effective solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M274 engine prices for your Mercedes V200 / V250

problems.h4: M274 High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why the V200 / V250 Cuts Out Suddenly
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes V Class V200, V250, V260 (M274.920, 2014-present)
problems.rootCause: The M274's camshaft-driven high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) operates at up to 200 bar. Internal wear - particularly to the pump piston and cam follower - reduces fuel pressure to the direct injection rails, triggering limp mode or complete engine cut-out. Contaminated fuel accelerates wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP, flush fuel system, replace fuel filter, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught immediately after first cut-out

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: HPFP replacement plus injector testing and rail inspection for metal debris
repairOptions.longevity: Required if HPFP has contaminated the fuel rail

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M274 with new HPFP, injectors, high-pressure rails, timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when metal debris has destroyed camshaft lobes

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V200 or V250 worth £15,000-£35,000, the HPFP replacement at £500-£800 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if metal debris has caused additional damage.
problems.recommendation: If your V Class petrol has cut out once but restarted, don't gamble. Replace the HPFP at a specialist immediately - £500-£800 is far cheaper than replacing injectors or an entire engine. On higher-mileage M274 units with over 90,000 miles, a full rebuilt engine with new HPFP and timing components eliminates all common failure points in one go.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M274 Mercedes V Class V200 / V250 engine prices

problems.group: M274 Carbon Buildup & Camshaft Actuator Wear
problems.h4: M274 Carbon Buildup & Camshaft Actuator Wear - Why the V Class Petrol Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes V Class V200, V250, V260 (M274.920, 2014-present)
problems.rootCause: The M274's direct injection system means fuel does not wash the intake valves, allowing carbon deposits to accumulate over time. This leads to misfires, rough idle, and loss of power. Camshaft actuator wear can also cause ticking on cold start and, in severe cases, camshaft failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blast intake valves, clean throttle body, reset adaptations
Replace camshaft actuators with updated parts
repairOptions.longevity: If ticking on cold start or fault codes present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M274 with new camshafts, actuators, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for catastrophic camshaft failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a V Class V200 or V250 worth £15,000-£35,000, walnut blasting at £300-£500 is excellent preventative maintenance. Camshaft actuator replacement at £450-£750 is also justified. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The M274's carbon buildup is an inherent trait of direct-injection petrol engines - budget for walnut blasting every 60,000 miles to maintain performance and fuel economy. If you hear ticking on cold start, have the camshaft actuators inspected immediately; updated parts resolve the issue.
